1: The first MLB game in the archive turned into an 11-inning, 1–0 Dodger Stadium classic—and a remarkably dense time capsule. Four future Hall of Famers shared the field: [[134181|Adrian Beltré]], [[115749|Rickey Henderson]], [[123833|Larry Walker]] and [[115732|Todd Helton]].

For 10 innings, neither side could break through. [[111554|Kevin Brown]] gave Los Angeles eight scoreless innings, allowing three hits with six strikeouts, while Colorado starter [[276336|Shawn Chacon]] matched him with seven scoreless frames and six strikeouts. [[150378|Eric Gagne]] struck out three in a clean ninth to keep the game even.

The Dodgers finally finished it in the 11th. [[133321|Alex Cora]] singled and scored the only run when [[115094|Shawn Green]] lined a walk-off single to center. Green went 2-for-5 with the RBI, sending the archive’s first MLB night home on a one-run walk-off.
2: Cincinnati and Los Angeles traded first-inning runs, with [[115135|Ken Griffey Jr.]] bringing home Ryan Freel on a sacrifice fly before César Izturis answered with a solo homer. The tie did not last long.

[[150178|Jason LaRue]] delivered the decisive swing in the second, a three-run homer that put the Reds ahead for good. He added a two-run shot in the ninth, finishing 2-for-3 with two home runs, five RBI and two runs scored in a 6–1 Cincinnati win.

[[407799|Brandon Claussen]] handled the rest from the mound, holding the Dodgers to one run on four hits across seven innings with five strikeouts. [[434885|D.J. Houlton]] struck out four over six innings for Los Angeles, but the two LaRue homers supplied nearly all the separation Cincinnati needed.
3: Los Angeles and Toronto played an 11-inning back-and-forth at Angel Stadium. The Angels opened the scoring in the second when [[115223|Vladimir Guerrero]] came home on an error, but the Blue Jays answered in the fifth on [[407861|Orlando Hudson]]’s RBI double before [[408210|Chone Figgins]] put Los Angeles back in front later that inning.

The lead changed again in a three-run Toronto seventh. Hudson’s second RBI of the night started the surge, and the Blue Jays went ahead 4–3. Figgins’ eighth-inning forceout brought home [[430895|Maicer Izturis]] to tie it, setting up extra innings after the bullpens kept the score level.

In the 11th, [[111851|Orlando Cabrera]] singled and came around on [[113889|Darin Erstad]]’s walk-off single to left. [[150456|Adam Kennedy]] supplied a 4-for-5 night with an RBI, while [[276912|Scot Shields]] worked two scoreless innings to earn the win in the 5–4 Angels finish.
4: The Dodgers did all their scoring in the first inning against San Diego, capitalizing on a Mark Loretta error before [[425854|Oscar Robles]] drove a double into right. [[430632|Willy Aybar]] and [[400292|Hee-Seop Choi]] both scored on the play, giving Los Angeles a three-run cushion before the game settled into a pitching duel.

[[117955|Derek Lowe]] made the early lead stand. He limited the Padres to one run across 7.2 innings, scattering seven hits with four strikeouts. San Diego finally got on the board in the eighth, when [[137001|Robert Fick]] singled home [[150353|Dave Roberts]], but could not produce another breakthrough.

[[400093|Duaner Sánchez]] entered to get the final four outs and earned the save, preserving a 3–1 Dodgers win. The game’s only two scoring plays came seven innings apart, with Lowe’s start giving Los Angeles exactly the room it needed.
5: A 13-inning game at Angel Stadium featured three future Hall of Famers—[[400085|Ichiro Suzuki]], [[134181|Adrian Beltré]] and [[115223|Vladimir Guerrero]]—and an early Angels lead that would not hold. Guerrero opened the scoring with a second-inning homer, then came around again during Los Angeles’ three-run third, capped by [[121640|Tim Salmon]]’s two-run single.

Seattle fought back from a 4–1 deficit. [[435358|Yuniesky Betancourt]] homered in the third, Beltré reached on an error that scored Carl Everett in the fourth, and [[430598|Jeremy Reed]] tied it with a solo homer in the fifth. The score stayed 4–4 for seven full innings as both bullpens absorbed the extra-inning workload.

[[122027|Richie Sexson]] finally broke through in the 13th with a solo homer to center. [[430941|George Sherrill]] delivered two scoreless innings for the win, and [[430646|Jake Woods]] finished the 5–4 Seattle victory with a scoreless 13th for the save.
6: Atlanta and New York played a 12-inning game that swung twice after the eighth. [[116662|Andruw Jones]] put the Braves ahead in the fourth with a double that scored [[121074|Edgar Renteria]], and [[435263|Brian McCann]] made it 2–0 in the sixth with an RBI single after [[116706|Chipper Jones]] reached home.

The Yankees chipped away. [[121347|Alex Rodriguez]] grounded out to score Melky Cabrera in the sixth, then [[114739|Jason Giambi]]’s eighth-inning solo homer forced extra innings. [[122477|John Smoltz]] gave Atlanta seven innings of one-run ball with five strikeouts, while [[425426|Chien-Ming Wang]] matched him with eight innings and two earned runs allowed.

[[279578|Marcus Giles]] briefly put Atlanta back in front with a 12th-inning homer, but New York had the final answer. Kevin Reese reached, and Rodriguez ended it with a two-run walk-off homer to left off [[407901|Jorge Sosa]], giving the Yankees a 4–3 finish.
7: Washington grabbed the game’s first run in the third when [[150479|Felipe López]] drove his 11th homer of the season to right. San Diego’s [[432934|Chris Young]] kept the game close into the middle innings, but the Nationals’ order found its decisive separation the next time through.

[[150093|Alfonso Soriano]] doubled home Marlon Anderson in the fifth, then Washington broke it open with a four-run sixth. [[475582|Ryan Zimmerman]] launched a two-run homer, [[400290|Austin Kearns]] doubled in Nick Johnson and [[425508|Ryan Church]] followed with an RBI single to make it 6–1.

San Diego produced its two runs on [[408036|Josh Bard]]’s fifth-inning RBI single and [[425468|Rob Bowen]]’s solo homer in the sixth, but never closed the gap. [[150009|Ramón Ortiz]] worked six innings for the win, while the Nationals’ bullpen supplied three scoreless innings in a 6–2 Washington finish at PETCO Park.
8: The Angels opened the scoring when [[407487|Juan Rivera]] hit his 21st homer in the second, but Boston countered with a two-run third. David Ortiz and Kevin Youkilis scored when [[276377|Wily Mo Peña]] reached on a Chone Figgins error, putting the Red Sox ahead despite the play producing no RBI.

Los Angeles immediately answered. [[110236|Garret Anderson]] grounded out to bring home [[111851|Orlando Cabrera]] in the third, and [[408210|Chone Figgins]]’ fourth-inning single scored Robb Quinlan for a 3–2 lead. [[425903|Kevin Youkilis]] doubled in Ortiz to tie it in the seventh, but Anderson’s bottom-half single brought [[115223|Vladimir Guerrero]] home with the deciding run.

[[434578|Joe Saunders]] held Boston to two unearned runs over 5.2 innings, and [[276912|Scot Shields]] earned the win after allowing the tying run in the seventh. Guerrero doubled twice and scored twice, while [[408061|Francisco Rodríguez]] worked the ninth for the save in a 4–3 Angels victory.
9: Toronto and Los Angeles traded two-run first innings at Dodger Stadium. [[122644|Matt Stairs]] doubled home Alex Rios, and Stairs came in on a double-play grounder before the Dodgers answered on RBI hits from [[114935|Luis Gonzalez]] and [[425766|James Loney]].

The Blue Jays separated themselves in the middle innings. [[136880|Roy Halladay]] helped his own cause with an RBI single in the second, then [[136267|Troy Glaus]] doubled home Vernon Wells in the third before [[150348|John McDonald]] added an RBI single. Glaus hit solo homers in both the fifth and sixth, while McDonald, Sal Fasano and Rios combined to drive in three more during a five-run fifth.

Halladay earned the win with seven innings of three-run ball, and Toronto closed out an 11–5 victory. Glaus went 3-for-4 with two homers, three runs and two RBI; McDonald finished 3-for-4 with two runs and two RBI. Gonzalez doubled twice and drove in three for the Dodgers, including a two-run ninth-inning double.
10: The Freeway Series matchup stayed scoreless through four innings before the Angels finally broke through against [[121834|Jason Schmidt]]. With the bases loaded in the fifth, [[435065|Reggie Willits]] lined a single to right that scored [[115223|Vladimir Guerrero]] and Gary Matthews Jr., then [[435062|Howie Kendrick]] singled in Casey Kotchman for all three runs of the night.

[[450308|Jered Weaver]] made that fifth-inning outburst stand. He worked 5.1 scoreless innings, yielding four hits while striking out three. Darren Oliver got the final two outs of the sixth, and [[276912|Scot Shields]] added two scoreless innings to hand the ninth to [[408061|Francisco Rodríguez]].

Rodríguez struck out all three Dodgers he faced for the save, completing a 3–0 Angels win. Willits reached three times on a hit and two walks to go with his two RBI, while the Dodgers could not convert five walks and six hits into a run.
11: Atlanta carried a 1–0 lead into the middle innings after [[121074|Edgar Renteria]] singled home Scott Thorman in the third. [[122477|John Smoltz]] protected that advantage through four, but the Dodgers finally broke through in the fifth when [[431145|Russell Martin]] doubled home Rafael Furcal.

Los Angeles moved in front for good in the sixth. [[461314|Matt Kemp]] hit a two-run homer, scoring James Loney, and the Dodgers then turned the seventh into a five-run surge. Martin singled in Juan Pierre, [[116999|Jeff Kent]] brought Martin home, and a Chipper Jones throwing error, Kemp’s bases-loaded walk and an Olmedo Sáenz sacrifice fly completed the rally.

[[346847|Joe Beimel]] worked two scoreless innings to earn the win after Derek Lowe’s five-inning start, and the Dodgers finished an 8–2 victory. Martin went 4-for-5 with two RBI, while Kemp drove in three; Renteria’s two RBI accounted for both Atlanta runs.
12: A 22-run game began with a six-run Mets first inning. [[431151|David Wright]] doubled home two, Ramón Castro added an RBI single, and former Dodger [[115094|Shawn Green]] singled in two more on a play that included a Matt Kemp error before [[430905|Ruben Gotay]] made it 6–0. Los Angeles immediately answered with Luis Gonzalez’s two-run single, then Kemp’s two-run homer in the second cut the deficit to two.

New York rebuilt the lead with three runs in the third, including a José Reyes RBI groundout and [[136724|Marlon Anderson]]’s two-run single. The Dodgers stayed in the game through [[116999|Jeff Kent]]’s solo homer and an Olmedo Sáenz sacrifice fly, but the Mets added single runs on Reyes’ fifth-inning hit, [[113232|Carlos Delgado]]’s sixth-inning homer, Castro’s solo shot and [[136860|Carlos Beltrán]]’s eighth-inning homer.

The Dodgers kept scoring—Wilson Betemit, Furcal and Loney each drove in late runs—but New York held on for a 13–9 win. [[121986|Aaron Sele]] supplied the winning relief with three innings, while Gotay went 3-for-4 with two runs and an RBI; Kemp had a 2-for-5, three-run, two-RBI night in the loss.
13: Arizona opened the series at PETCO Park with a power-driven second inning. [[452220|Stephen Drew]] launched a two-run homer to right-center after [[433582|Conor Jackson]] doubled, giving the Diamondbacks an early lead against [[430683|Justin Germano]].

The margin grew to four in the fifth when [[455759|Chris Young]] followed [[435041|Carlos Quentin]] with another two-run homer. That was all the support Arizona needed; Young and Drew each supplied a home run and two RBI in a game with only two scoring plays.

[[425630|Brandon Webb]] made the four-run cushion stand with seven scoreless innings, allowing three hits and two walks while striking out seven. [[407193|Brandon Lyon]] and [[430963|Ramón Peña]] finished the 4–0 shutout; [[150396|Milton Bradley]] recorded two of San Diego’s three hits.
14: The next night began as a low-scoring game. San Diego’s [[150396|Milton Bradley]] brought home [[111904|Mike Cameron]] with a fourth-inning groundout, but Arizona took its first lead in the fifth when [[452249|Micah Owings]] doubled in [[237800|Jeff DaVanon]] and [[455759|Chris Young]] followed with an RBI double.

Arizona extended the lead to 5–1 in the sixth. [[430965|Chris Snyder]] singled home [[291565|Eric Byrnes]] and [[433582|Conor Jackson]], then DaVanon’s sacrifice fly brought [[448602|Mark Reynolds]] home. Owings went 2-for-3 at the plate and delivered six innings of one-run ball on the mound.

The Padres roared back with four in the ninth—[[150398|Geoff Blum]] doubled in a run, Cameron singled home Blum, and Bradley tied it with a two-run homer. Arizona had the last response in the 11th: Byrnes singled in DaVanon, then [[429710|Chad Tracy]] hit a three-run homer to seal a 9–5 Diamondbacks win. [[407878|José Valverde]] earned the win after two innings of relief.
15: Chicago raced to a four-run first at Wrigley Field, stringing together four RBI doubles. [[136660|Mark DeRosa]] scored [[444135|Ryan Theriot]], [[133380|Aramis Ramírez]] brought DeRosa home, then [[444844|Jake Fox]] and [[150218|Jacque Jones]] added consecutive run-scoring doubles to build a 4–0 lead.

Cincinnati immediately drew even in the second. [[276055|Adam Dunn]] opened the inning with a solo homer, then the Reds loaded the bases for [[285078|Josh Hamilton]]’s RBI hit-by-pitch, [[433898|Jeff Keppinger]]’s RBI single and [[115135|Ken Griffey Jr.]]’s run-scoring single. DeRosa put Chicago ahead for good with a fourth-inning RBI single.

The Cubs broke the tie open with seven runs in the seventh: Jones singled in a run, Theriot doubled in two, DeRosa singled in two and Ramírez added another RBI double. DeRosa finished 5-for-5 with four RBI, while Jones and Ramírez each collected four hits in a 12–4 win. [[150302|Jason Marquis]] earned the decision after six innings, and Chicago’s bullpen closed with three scoreless frames.
16: Colorado struck first when [[425548|Garrett Atkins]] hit a two-run first-inning homer that scored [[407812|Matt Holliday]], but the Dodgers responded with one of the archive’s wildest opening frames. Los Angeles sent 14 men to the plate and scored 10 times against [[150230|Mark Redman]].

[[461314|Matt Kemp]] began the answer with a sacrifice fly, then [[116662|Andruw Jones]] drew a bases-loaded walk, [[455088|Blake DeWitt]] singled home two and [[207267|Brad Penny]] helped his own cause with an RBI single. [[279577|Rafael Furcal]] added an RBI double before Kemp capped the inning with a grand slam, scoring Penny, Furcal and [[334393|Juan Pierre]].

[[115732|Todd Helton]] singled home Willy Taveras in the sixth for Colorado’s final run, and [[434704|Delwyn Young]] answered with a seventh-inning RBI single for Los Angeles. Penny went 2-for-3 with an RBI and worked seven innings for the win, allowing three runs on four hits in an 11–3 Dodgers rout.
